glosses: Rassembler.
Dinge, die an verschiedenen Orten liegen, zu einem gemeinsamen Ort tragen

examples.text: Nach getaner Arbeit sammelte die Fußpflegerin ihr Arbeitszeug zusammen und fuhr zur nächsten Kundin.
Die Exponate wurden in jahrzehntelanger Kleinarbeit zusammengesammelt und werden nun erstmals gemeinsam ausgestellt.

translations.source_sense_description: Dinge, die an verschiedenen Orten liegen, zu einem gemeinsamen Ort tragen

glosses: To collect normally separate things.

examples.text: I've been gathering ideas from the people I work with.
She bent down to gather the reluctant cat from beneath the chair.

glosses: To collect normally separate things.
Especially, to harvest food.

examples.text: We went to gather some blackberries from the nearby lane.

glosses: To collect normally separate things.
To accumulate over time, to amass little by little.

examples.text: Over the years he'd gathered a considerable collection of mugs.

glosses: To collect normally separate things.
To congregate, or assemble.

examples.text: People gathered round as he began to tell his story.
Tears from the depth of some divine despair / Rise in the heart, and gather to the eyes, […]

At the north-western most of Iran, to the south of Maku, is the Church of Qara Kelisa (meaning the Black Church) in a village of the same name. Here is reputed to be the burialplace of St. Thaddeus and every year thousands of Armenians gather there for prayer.

glosses: To collect normally separate things.
To grow gradually larger by accretion.

examples.text: Their snow-ball did not gather as it went.

glosses: To bring parts of a whole closer.

examples.text: She gathered the shawl about her as she stepped into the cold.

glosses: To bring parts of a whole closer.
To add pleats or folds to a piece of cloth, normally to reduce its width.

examples.text: A gown should be gathered around the top so that it will remain shaped.

glosses: To bring parts of a whole closer.
To bring stitches closer together.

examples.text: Be careful not to stretch or gather your knitting.
If you want to emphasise the shape, it is possible to gather the waistline.

glosses: To bring parts of a whole closer.
To bring together, or nearer together, in masonry, as for example where the width of a fireplace is rapidly diminished to the width of the flue.
To bring parts of a whole closer.
To haul in; to take up.

examples.text: to gather the slack of a rope

glosses: To infer or conclude; to know from a different source.

examples.text: From his silence, I gathered that things had not gone well.
I gather from Aunty May that you had a good day at the match.

Press reports of the length of time the bridge is likely to be out of action vary greatly, but Mr. Farr gathers that a temporary structure may be ready in six months; complete reconstruction, however, will take at least two years. [It was never rebuilt or replaced, and demolished instead.]

glosses: To be filled with pus

examples.text: Salt water can help boils to gather and then burst.

glosses: To collect molten glass on the end of a tool.
To gain; to win.

examples.text: He gathers ground upon her in the chase.

glosses: A plait or fold in cloth, made by drawing a thread through it; a pucker.
The inclination forward of the axle journals to keep the wheels from working outward.
The soffit or under surface of the masonry required in gathering. See gather.
A blob of molten glass collected on the end of a blowpipe.
A gathering.

examples.text: "I'll tell you all about it at the Gather, win or lose."
What bothered him more, he thought as he started Washoe southward, was Spikes's animosity, the bearded man's sudden violent reaction to his arrival at the gather.

translations.source_sense_description: Dinge, die an verschiedenen Orten liegen, zu einem gemeinsamen Ort tragen

glosses: Assembler de nouveau des personnes, des bêtes ou des choses qui étaient dispersées.

examples.text: Le père et la fille ne se rassemblaient plus qu’aux heures des repas.
Debout à nouveau, il rassembla ses esprits et se dirigea vers la galerie.
L’été avait dispersé les personnes de notre société, l’hiver les rassemble.
Nous avons été longtemps séparés, le sort nous rassemble.

glosses: Mettre ensemble, unir ou assembler ce qui était épars.

examples.text: Rassembler des preuves contre un accusé, ou pour prouver ce que l’on avance.
Je suis incapable de rassembler deux idées ; votre vue m’a ébloui. Je ne pense plus, j’admire.

Mathilde ramassa un des râteau et se mit à rassembler l’herbe couchée en un tas, prenant soin que son coup de râteau ramasse les tiges perpendiculairement à la fauchée de Jean pour ordonner le tas en fibres parallèles.

Chaque fois que cela était possible, on se rassemblait à quelques-uns sur la place des marronniers autour de celui qui était parvenu à chiper une ou deux cibiches dans le paquet paternel ou dans celui d'un aïeul.

glosses: Assembler des forces militaires.

examples.text: A cette nouvelle, on rassembla toutes les troupes et on marcha aux ennemis.

glosses: Mettre ensemble un cheval ; agir simultanément des mains et des jambes, de manière que le cheval, s’asseyant sur les hanches, ait le devant plus libre pour l’exécution des mouvements.

examples.text: Rassemblez votre cheval.

glosses: Remettre dans l’état où elles étaient des pièces de menuiserie on de charpente qui ont été désassemblées.

examples.text: On a démonté cette charpente, il faut la rassembler.

glosses: Position du cheval appuyé sur les postérieurs, dont le devant est plus libre pour l’exécution des mouvements.

examples.text: Beaucoup d'écuyers veulent que la tête du cheval soit ployée sur l'encolure en dedans, […]. Nous ferons remarquer que cette position ployée nuit au rassembler.
